title: Chanan the Tailor
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Avodah Zarah 39a, Rav Huna bar Minyomi bought tekhelet from members of Rav Amram Chasida’s household and came before Rav Yosef, who did not have [an answer]. Chanan the tailor met him and said to him: “What does Yosef the poor know? A case happened to me: I bought tekhelet from members of the household of Ravnai, the brother of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, and I came before Rav Mattenah, who did not have [an answer]. I came before Rav Yehudah of Hagronia (in Rabbeinu Chananel and Dikdukei Soferim the word ‘of Hagronia’ is absent), who said to me, ‘You have fallen into my hand,’” etc. Hyman explains this as what Yuchasin meant in writing “chapter HaTekhelet”: it means that he is mentioned in connection with the law of tekhelet.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Avodah Zarah39a fully writes the subsequent Chanan/RavMattenah/RavYehudah chain. Hyman’s reading without ofHagronia and his interpretation of Yuchasin’s chapter title remain attributed; the source’s תיתב is read as תיבת.

The consulted Avodah Zarah 39a directly preserves Chanan the tailor and the Rav Mattenah/Rav Yehudah chain. Hyman’s reported omission of Hagronia in Rabbeinu Chananel and Dikdukei Soferim, and his interpretation of Yuchasin’s chapter reference, remain attributed.
